entity: The Crowd Counting Consortium (CCC), a joint project of Harvard Kennedy School and the University of Connecticut, part of the Nonviolent Action Lab at the Ash Center, begun in 2017 by Jeremy Pressman (UConn) and Erica Chenoweth (HKS) to estimate the participants in the Women's March of 21 January 2017, which collects publicly available data on political protest events reported in the United States and publishes them monthly on the Harvard Dataverse (ash.harvard.edu/programs/crowd-counting-consortium/); formalized in the maryleelabor left-and-labor census record of 2026-10-31 (https://www.maryleelabor.org/aggregators/crowd-counting-consortium/)
row_type: C (a public entity on which the archive bears: a university project publishing a protest-event dataset; an entity of the maryleelabor left-and-labor census, area labor-action)

The census's own unit ('a political protest event reported in the United States, with crowd numbers'), evidence_kind ('event dataset') and area ('labor-action': 'strikes, stoppages and protest events, counted and described') for the entity (ML record, census.json rows[slug == 'crowd-counting-consortium'].unit, .evidence_kind, .areas; areas['labor-action']).

classes_note: Two classes, each stated by field sources at the loci given and by the census's own unit, evidence kind, area and operator for the entity: (1) protest event data, the consortium's unit and evidence kind (B1, B3, B6; census unit, evidence_kind 'event dataset', area 'labor-action'); (2) nonviolent action and civil resistance, the consortium's institutional home (the Nonviolent Action Lab) and a category its page applies to the events it counts (B1, B3, B4; census operator). The census area 'labor-action' is the census's placement; its negative tag reads 'NOT a labor dataset: it records political protest of every kind, and labor action only as part of it', so labor action as such (strikes, stoppages) is no class of the entity and enters no class pass; the archive's labor instruments (DSL, #771; the directionality stack; user labor drag) bear on labor performed with AI and on none of the two classes. #1725 (Ils ne sont pas marxistes, AXN:0B50), the census's anchor, is read at its passages on datasets of the left, holders and the losing side (its 'One caution applies to the whole sample' passage, its Conclusion and its Gaps); its organ/holder/route conditions concern the record of disputes inside left organizations, and the census's reading that applies the holder to the consortium is the archive's reading, ledgered as ML-NN, and enters no class pass. The aliases are the entity's name, its handle and site name (crowdcounting, crowdcounting.org, @crowdcounting, the Dataverse slug crowdcountingconsortium) and its blog's name (Counting Crowds, case-sensitive); 'CCC' is not used, being too short to match only the entity. Erica Chenoweth, Jeremy Pressman and Jay Ulfelder are persons distinct from the entity; the Nonviolent Action Lab and the Ash Center are its institutional home, entities distinct from it; Count Love (countlove.org) is a collaborator, an entity distinct from it; crowd counting as the estimation of crowd sizes (the Wikipedia article 'Crowd counting') is a homonym of the name's common noun. Admission by reading (§3.4): D where a deposit names the entity and says something of it; O-class where a sentence applies an archive category to protest event data or to nonviolent action as a class; a bare mention, a figural use of 'counting', a list of keywords or a reference line is not a claim.
